newsitem.title: CUBA: Cuba preparing new law on insurance sector.
newsitem.headline: Cuba preparing new law on insurance sector.

text.p: Cuba is preparing a new law to update its regulations on insurance that may include the possibility of foreign investment in the sector, a senior Cuban official said Tuesday.
Finance Minister Manual Millares, speaking to foreign reporters, did not however give details of the law or when it would be approved.

The planned law would be in line with Cuba's policy of economic reform over the past three years that has included new laws on foreign investment, taxation and free trade zones and a restructuring of the country's banking system.
Foreign insurance firms are not currently permitted to operate commercially in Cuba.

Millares, who was attending an international conference of insurance companies from developing countries in Havana, also noted the Cuban insurance sector could suffer the effects of recent U.S. legislation to tighten the longstanding economic embargo against Cuba.
This was because any falling off of international business due to the Helms-Burton law -- which seeks to discourage foreign investment in Cuba -- was bound to cut into the insurance sector, he said.
Cuba's insurance sector, nationalized following the 1959 communist revolution, consists of several state firms providing coverages from marine and aviation through farm and financial insurance.
The personal insurance market for cover such as personal sickness or accidents is only just beginning to emerge and has so far been confined to foreign tourists and residents.
